//: Reviewed npm-audit exceptions: pnpm workspace (pnpm-lock.yaml).
An entry here suppresses ONE advisory id on ONE package name in the CI
dependency audit (scripts/security/check-npm-audit.sh, HIGH+CRITICAL gate).
The bar for adding one is high. The advisory must have NO fixed release to
upgrade to. The advisory must also not be exploitable in production, by
one of two bars. Either the package is absent from the production
dependency closure of every shipped workspace package
(`pnpm -r why <pkg> --prod`) and from every built artifact, with that
evidence in the PR; or present in a production closure only where
the vulnerable function is provably never called at runtime, with a
negative runtime test and a positive control, both recorded in the entry
(in its `reason`). A public tracking issue must exist so the entry is
removed the moment a fixed release ships. An advisory with an available fix
must be fixed by upgrading (or a pnpm override), never listed here.
Enforced by check-npm-audit.sh on every run: exact id + package match only;
every entry is printed; an entry past `expires` fails the run even after
the advisory disappears; `expires` may be at most 30 days out, so renewing
an entry means re-reviewing it; a malformed or missing file fails the run.
Entry format:
id       OSV/GHSA id exactly as osv-scanner reports it
package  npm package name exactly as osv-scanner reports it
reason   which bar applies and the evidence for it (for the second bar, the negative runtime test and positive control), and the tracking issue as #<number>
expires  YYYY-MM-DD (UTC), the last day the exception is honoured
